overview.title: Gender Inequality Index Global Gender Gap Index Gender Parity Index Comparison
overview.definition: A comprehensive comparative study of three premier global indices—Gender Inequality Index (GII by UNDP), Global Gender Gap Index (GGGI by WEF), and Gender Parity Index (GPI by UNESCO)—evaluating gender disparities across reproductive health, empowerment, economic participation, and education.
overview.importanceInUpsc: Crucial for UPSC CSE Prelims (factual criteria, publishing agencies, indicator sets) and Mains GS Paper-1 (Women's role, population, developmental issues) and GS Paper-2 (Inclusive governance, social sector policies, international reports).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts, indicator methodologies, and publishing agencies of GII, GGGI, and GPI.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and India's latest rankings and performance trajectories.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims statements and construct value-added Mains arguments.
prerequisites: Basic concepts of Human Development Index (HDI)
Understanding of socio-economic gender disparities in India

sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Foundational Principle 1**: **Gender Inequality Index (GII)** introduced by UNDP in HDR 2010 measures human development losses due to gender inequality across three dimensions: **reproductive health, empowerment, and the labour market**.
• **Foundational Principle 2**: **Global Gender Gap Index (GGGI)** published by the World Economic Forum (WEF) since 2006 benchmarks national gender parity across four pillars: **Economic Participation, Educational Attainment, Health and Survival, and Political Empowerment**.
• **Foundational Principle 3**: **Gender Parity Index (GPI)** is a socioeconomic index usually designed by UNESCO measuring the ratio of female-to-male values of a given indicator (e.g., gross enrolment ratio in education).
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Directionality of indices: GII ranges from 0 (equality) to 1 (total inequality), whereas GGGI ranges from 0 (parity/inequality depending on formulation, actually WEF scale is 0 to 1 where 1 represents complete gender parity).

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Published by UNDP in Human Development Report. Focuses on health, empowerment, and labour.
Uses maternal mortality ratio, adolescent birth rate, parliamentary seats, secondary education attainment, labour force participation rate.
Frequent Prelims questions on dimensions and publisher; highlights structural losses in human development.
Published annually by World Economic Forum (WEF), Geneva. Compares countries regardless of development level.
Measures gaps between women and men across 4 sub-indices: Economic, Education, Health, Political.
India's ranking trends (e.g., performance in political empowerment vs economic participation) are high-yield for Mains.
Promoted heavily by UNESCO for education sector monitoring (SDG 4).
Calculated as Female Value divided by Male Value. Value of 1 indicates complete parity; <1 disparity in favour of males; >1 in favour of females.
Used in educational statistics, Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) analysis in Economic Survey and AISHE reports.

items.definition: Measured via Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) and Adolescent Birth Rate (ABR); captures health risks specific to women.
Captured by the proportion of parliamentary seats occupied by females and population with at least secondary education by gender.
Measures participation rate in economic activity; India's low Female Labour Force Participation Rate (FLFPR) severely impacts GII and GGGI scores.
Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, National Food Security Act, Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act 2017, and recommendations of the High-Level Committee on Status of Women (2015).

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Nordic Advantage**: Iceland, Finland, Norway consistently top GGGI due to robust parental leave, childcare support, and political representation.
• **South Asian Realities**: High gender gaps persist in South Asia driven by patriarchal norms, safety concerns, and uneven economic opportunities.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Unpaid care work burden, digital gender divide, safety and security in public spaces, occupational segregation.
• **Policy Interventions**: Institutionalized skilling via National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM), conditional cash transfers, gender-responsive budgeting.

items.title: Mnemonic for GGGI Four Pillars
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: "PEHP" -> **P**olitical, **E**conomic, **H**ealth, **P**aternal/Education (Think: **P**olitical **E**conomists **H**eal **P**eople).
• **Decoded Meaning**: **P**olitical Empowerment, **E**conomic Participation & Opportunity, **H**ealth & Survival, **E**ducational Attainment.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly spots intruder indicators in MCQ options.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: **UNDP = GII (Health-Empowerment-Labour)** | **WEF = GGGI (4 Pillars)** | **UNESCO = GPI (Ratio)**.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently interchanges publishing bodies, such as stating that the World Bank publishes the Global Gender Gap Index (it is published by the World Economic Forum) or that GII measures absolute equality (it measures percentage loss in human development due to inequality).

Mains Value Addition: In GS-1 and GS-2 answers regarding women empowerment, cite WEF's GGGI findings specifically noting India's stellar performance in Political Empowerment countered by structural lags in Economic Participation and Opportunity.

keyTakeaways: GII by UNDP measures human development loss via Reproductive Health, Empowerment, and Labour Market.
GGGI by WEF uses 4 comprehensive pillars, with political empowerment being a major strength for India and economic gap remaining a challenge.
GPI is a straightforward ratio (<1, 1, >1) extensively utilized in educational metrics like GER.
